problem.scope: Provide snapshot isolation and schema evolution over immutable data objects and an ordered transaction log. Compare backend-supported conditional commit creation with an external commit coordinator. S3 currently supports conditional writes; neither design assumes atomic directory rename or append.

evidence.testName: L044 conditional create commits once, rebases disjoint writers and aborts slow writers through the log

acceptanceCases.given: Writers A and B with overlapping predicates and a disjoint writer C all read version 4; writer D staged files long before cleanup runs.
acceptanceCases.then: Only A owns version 5; B conflicts; C rebases to version 6; D aborts because the marker precedes its commit, so its deleted files are never referenced.
acceptanceCases.when: A creates version 5, B and C retry, cleanup creates an abort marker for D, then D tries to commit.

acceptanceCases.given: Two writers target the same version key after reading one snapshot.
acceptanceCases.then: Only one creates that immutable version; loser rereads and revalidates conflict predicates.

acceptanceCases.given: A reader pins version 12 while version 13 commits and checkpoint 10 is available.
acceptanceCases.then: Read version 12 consistently without mixing new metadata or requiring directory rename.

evidence.testName: L044 conditional create commits once, rebases disjoint writers and aborts slow writers through the log

acceptanceCases.given: An old snapshot still references a data file while transaction D's uncommitted upload ages past grace.
acceptanceCases.then: Referenced files stay; D's upload is deleted only after an abort marker commits in the log, and D's later commit attempt aborts instead of referencing deleted files.
acceptanceCases.when: Run cleanup with the active-reader floor, then let D try to commit.
